capabilities: search the open note and highlight every match in place
step through matches with Enter, Shift+Enter or arrows
scroll to the current match only when it is off screen
switch to reading view while editing and restore the previous mode afterwards
fall back to the command palette until Cmd+F is freed
extras: Requires a one-time manual hotkey change to free Cmd+F from built-in search (the plugin never edits hotkey settings itself); highlighting depends on the CSS Custom Highlight API being present in the device web engine, and the author states it has not been tested on a physical phone. Matches in unrendered parts of very long notes are counted only as they scroll into view.
intentEvidence: Obsidian's built-in Cmd+F lives inside the editor.
motivation: The author built it because the built-in editor search forces the editor to expose raw Markdown of the block containing a match, destroying the rendered view the user was looking at.
problem: Obsidian's built-in Cmd+F works in the editor, so highlighting a match exposes raw Markdown and collapses rendered tables into unreadable pipe walls.
summary: In-note search that highlights every match in the rendered reading view without unrendering tables, callouts or code blocks.
